ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle MNQ, Q, S, N are on the same straight line, and S is located on side QN. Segment MS connects from vertex M to point S. Point R is located near side QM, and segment SR divides angle QSM into two small angles: ∠2 is between SQ and SR, and ∠1 is between SR and SM. Reasoning: Because the problem gives that MS is an altitude of triangle MNQ, MS is perpendicular to QN. Since SQ is a part of QN, ∠QSM is a right angle, with measure 90°. In the figure, ∠1 and ∠2 together exactly form ∠QSM, so m∠1 + m∠2 = 90. Substitute m∠1 = 3x + 11 and m∠2 = 7x + 9 to get (3x + 11) + (7x + 9) = 90. Combine like terms: 10x + 20 = 90, so 10x = 70, x = 7.

raw_record.question_text: Find $x$ if $\overline{MS}$ is an altitude of $\triangle MNQ$, $m\angle 1 = 3x + 11$, and $m \angle 2 = 7x + 9$.

method.method_draft: From the image, note that Q, S, and N lie on the same straight side of triangle MNQ, and the ray SR lies inside the angle formed by SQ and SM. The labels show angle 2 between SQ and SR and angle 1 between SR and SM, so angles 1 and 2 together make angle QSM. From the text, MS is an altitude of triangle MNQ, so MS is perpendicular to QN; since SQ is part of QN, angle QSM is a right angle. Therefore m∠1 + m∠2 = 90. Substitute the text-given expressions: (3x + 11) + (7x + 9) = 90, then solve to get x = 7.
